evidenceFindings.finding: Democracy is limited by general constitutional law, private liberties and dispersed authority, rather than unchecked majority will.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Constitutional-liberal inference applies to this authority rule, not automatically to referendum or recall machinery.

evidenceFindings.finding: Protects a private sphere and tolerates beliefs/morals he personally rejects, under predictable general law.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified liberty inference addresses this coercion boundary; it does not settle every police procedure.

evidenceFindings.finding: Voluntary differing groups and customs permit experimental evolution; conformity need not be enforced.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Plural participation is inferred from voluntary customs, without assuming government funding or every legal exemption.

evidenceFindings.finding: Rejects a supranational currency monopoly but endorses a treaty eliminating currency/exchange barriers.
evidenceFindings.rationale: This monetary or treaty position is assessed individually; opposition to a monopoly is not blanket nationalism.

evidenceFindings.finding: Private property and competitive decentralized production are central; concession for genuine public functions remains.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified ownership inference for a competitive service avoids claiming all monopolies must be private.

evidenceFindings.finding: International trade, free currency/banking access and competition overcome national barriers.
evidenceFindings.rationale: General trade-doctrine inference is limited where the question invokes security or a precise external-subsidy exception.

evidenceFindings.finding: Dispersed knowledge and prices coordinate ordinary production; monetary competition opposes national monopoly and exchange controls.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Direct doctrinal application to this production/price/control proposition, with sector exceptions not silently assumed away.

evidenceFindings.finding: Rejects making outcomes equal as a definition of justice; tolerates basic assistance but stresses productive competition.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified distribution inference avoids treating minimum protection as zero public welfare or defining every tax instrument.

evidenceFindings.finding: Explicit religious tolerance and opposition to coercing private moral values; rejects supernatural authority as law.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Institutional-secular inference follows from noncoercion, not merely from personal religious belief.

evidenceFindings.finding: Rejects conservative fear of spontaneous change while defending evolved voluntary traditions and gradual experiments.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Evidence supports this specific attitude to evolving customs; modern sex/family policies remain separate.

evidenceFindings.finding: Innovation requires early adopters, creative destruction and workers adapting to new technology.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified AI-workplace analogy addresses displacement and adjustment; no clinical or embryo risk threshold is asserted.

evidenceFindings.finding: Learned conventions sustain cooperation; moral rules develop through cultural evolution and are not simply reasoned designs.
evidenceFindings.rationale: Qualified causal analogy is restricted to learned cooperative/moral conventions; no claim about stress, IQ or empathy heritability.

evidenceFindings.finding: Why I Am Not a Conservative expressly separates spiritual and temporal spheres and refuses supernatural authority as a political knowledge source.
evidenceFindings.rationale: An official religious review stage would mix the explicitly separated spheres, supporting qualified disagreement even when merely advisory. This does not forbid private religious citizens contributing opinions.
